sections.name: PLF

attrs.name: table
attrs.doc:
Height as a function of time. This is a list where each element has the form
     (TIME VALUE). The TIME entries must be increasing cronologically. The
     corresponding VALUE represents the value at that time. In order to find the
     depth for other times, linear interpolation between the entries in the list will
     be used.
        <    time value     >

sections.text:
Linear interpolation of depth.
  < PLF table ... >
    table: submodel (see section 4.1.7) sequence
     Height as a function of time. This is a list where each element has the form
     (TIME VALUE). The TIME entries must be increasing cronologically. The
     corresponding VALUE represents the value at that time. In order to find the
     depth for other times, linear interpolation between the entries in the list will
     be used.
        <    time value     >
        – time: Time fixed component (see section 107.27)
          Submodel (has partially specified default value)
          Time.
        – value: number [cm]
          Parameter
          Depth.

sections.name: file
sections.desc: Linear interpolation of depth read from file.

attrs.name: file
attrs.doc:
Name of file to read data from. The format of each line in the file is ’YEAR
        MONTH DAY HEIGHT’, where HEIGHT should in cm above ground (i.e. a
        negative number). Linear interpolation is used between the datapoints.

sections.text:
Linear interpolation of depth read from file.
  < file file >
       file: string (see section 4.1.5)
        Parameter
        Name of file to read data from. The format of each line in the file is ’YEAR
        MONTH DAY HEIGHT’, where HEIGHT should in cm above ground (i.e. a
        negative number). Linear interpolation is used between the datapoints.

sections.name: season
sections.desc: Linear interpolation of depth within a year.

attrs.name: season
attrs.doc: Depth as a function of Julian day. First and last entry must be identical.

sections.text:
Linear interpolation of depth within a year.
  < season season >
       season: plf [d → cm]
        Parameter
        Depth as a function of Julian day. First and last entry must be identical.

sections.name: table
sections.desc: Linear interpolation of depth read from file.
sections.sig:
< table (file file )
              (offset 0 [cm])
              (missing missing ...)           ; Has default value.
              (filter)
              (original original ...)
              (dim line dim line ) >

attrs.name: file
attrs.doc: Name of Daisy file where data is found.

attrs.name: offset
attrs.doc: Add this number to the Level read from the table.

attrs.name: missing
attrs.doc:
(missing "" "00.00")
    Parameter description:
    List of strings indicating missing values.

attrs.name: filter
attrs.doc:
Only include data from rows that passes all these filters.
       <   tag allowed ...      >

attrs.name: – tag
attrs.doc: Name of column in Daisy log file to filter for.

attrs.name: – allowed
attrs.doc: List of allowable values in filter.

attrs.name: original
attrs.doc:
List of dimensions of the data in the data file.
    If the list has only one element, that element is used as the dimension for
    all columns in the file. Otherwise, the list must have one element for each
    column.
    By default Daisy will use the names specified in data file.

attrs.name: dim line
attrs.doc:
If true, assume the line after the tags contain dimensions. By default this will
    be true iff ’original’ is not specified.

sections.text:
Linear interpolation of depth read from file.
  < table (file file )
              (offset 0 [cm])
              (missing missing ...)           ; Has default value.
              (filter)
              (original original ...)
              (dim line dim line ) >
       file: string (see section 4.1.5)
        Parameter
        Name of Daisy file where data is found.
       offset: number [cm]
        Parameter (default 0)
        Add this number to the Level read from the table.
       missing: string (see section 4.1.5) sequence
        Parameter (has default value with length 2)

        (missing "" "00.00")

    Parameter description:
    List of strings indicating missing values.
   filter : submodel (see section 4.1.7) sequence
    Submodel (default: an empty sequence)
    Only include data from rows that passes all these filters.
       <   tag allowed ...      >

       – tag: string (see section 4.1.5)
         Parameter
         Name of column in Daisy log file to filter for.
       – allowed : string (see section 4.1.5) sequence
         Parameter
         List of allowable values in filter.
   original : string (see section 4.1.5) sequence
    Optional parameter
    List of dimensions of the data in the data file.
    If the list has only one element, that element is used as the dimension for
    all columns in the file. Otherwise, the list must have one element for each
    column.
    By default Daisy will use the names specified in data file.
   dim line: boolean (see section 4.1.2)
    Optional parameter
    If true, assume the line after the tags contain dimensions. By default this will
    be true iff ’original’ is not specified.
